title: 한상 눈치해제
oneLiner: 각자 못 먹는 것·먹고 싶은 양·예산을 익명으로 눌러 공유 메뉴와 개인 메뉴, 굽기·보충 역할까지 20초에 합의하는 외식 테이블.
theme: 외로움 — belonging without silently sacrificing appetite or doing all the table labor.
targetUser: Korean family groups, mixed-preference friends, foreign residents, and barbecue restaurants.
keyUX: each diner privately taps avoid, crave, appetite, budget, and willingness to grill/refill; all reveal at once into a table map with individual exceptions and short role rotations.

sourceSignals.note: Shared-meal etiquette, appetite compromise, and table-labor discussion.

mechanic: sealed appetite chips reveal together, then a center plate composes shared and personal dishes plus rotating table roles.
triggerMoment: everyone has sat down but no one wants to be the difficult diner.
buyerShareAudience: restaurants, reservation services, group organizers, and diners.
userActionSentence: “못 먹는 것과 먹을 양은 남 눈치 안 보고 먼저 누르고 싶어요.”
threeSecondSting: four sealed diner chips around an empty table say “또 한 명이 다 굽고, 한 명은 덜 먹나요?”
outputArtifact: table agreement card with order split, portion assumptions, personal dishes, and role rotation.
firstValidationTest: run 20 mock four-person orders and compare discussion time, unchosen food, and role imbalance against ordinary verbal ordering.
lovedBySmallGroup: 4/5 — multigenerational families, mixed-diet friend groups, and visitors to Korean barbecue feel the friction immediately.
smallGroupFit: groups with allergies, small appetites, strict budgets, or recurring grill-duty resentment can decide in one meal whether it helps.
spreadTrigger: a graceful “everyone ate enough / roles rotated” table card can be shared with the group or restaurant.
referencePattern: anonymous party ballot + Korean shared-table ordering + round-robin chore token.
twist: it resolves invisible appetite and labor before menu optimization; nobody's private answer is attributed after reveal.
firstScreen: an empty round table with four sealed chips, one 20-second countdown, and no menu catalogue yet.
shareOrPlayLoop: invite diners → private chips → reveal → adjust one conflict → dine → share balanced-table card.
planBrief: User problem: shared dining etiquette hides hunger, dislikes, and labor. Inflow: table QR or reservation share. Business/validation: restaurant pilot priced per table or reservation integration. Core loop: join → private chips → reveal → compose → rotate roles → confirm. First screen: sealed diners, not a menu. Core screens: private input, reveal table, order composition, final card. Interaction rules: no answer attribution; one conflict at a time; diners can opt out. QA: two-person table, one abstention, allergy conflict, unequal budget, no shared dish, 390px mobile, Korean/English. Risk: the ritual must take less time than conversation.
developmentStartPrompt: Build a tabletop companion with four mocked diners, private preference states, synchronized reveal, shared-versus-personal dish composition, budget split, rotating grill/refill roles, one conflict resolution, and a shareable table agreement. Do not build a restaurant discovery or menu analytics dashboard.
stitchPrompt: Create a responsive Korean tabletop companion called “한상 눈치해제” for families, mixed-preference friends, foreign residents, and Korean barbecue restaurants. The observed pull is social: diners report eating less than they want while one person orders, grills, cuts, and refills for everyone. Open on an elegant empty round table with four sealed diner chips and one sentence: “또 한 명이 다 굽고, 한 명은 덜 먹나요?” Each diner privately chooses foods to avoid, one craving, appetite size, budget comfort, and whether they can grill or refill. Flip all chips together after 20 seconds, then compose shared dishes, personal exceptions, a fair budget split, and short rotating table roles. Show allergy conflict, abstention, unequal budget, no-shared-dish, and late-join states. Required sections: join, private chips, synchronized reveal, shared/personal plate map, budget, role rotation, conflict resolution, and final table card. Emotional pressure: belonging without hunger, shame, or invisible labor. Design direction: use the premium-editorial profile with warm paper, deep charcoal type, one muted persimmon accent, refined plate-like cards, 44px controls, gentle reveal motion, and no restaurant-discovery grid or analytics dashboard.
